reason: The cited evidence (E1) studies Y+Hf co-doping, not Hf alone, and reports reduced grain growth but does not measure spallation, HfO2 scale formation, or interfacial gradients. E2 concerns HfC coatings on a different substrate and is irrelevant to the HEA bond coat or oxidation mechanism. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior support or are misrepresented.
premises: Hf doping in AlCoCrFeNi-based HEA bond coats reduces oxide scale spallation by ~15–20%
Hf promotes formation of a dense, adherent HfO2 surface scale
Hf creates a compositional gradient at the coating–substrate interface that strengthens bonding
Hf doping refines grain structure and improves microstructural stability after heat treatment
The benefits are effective at 900 °C under molten salt hot corrosion (75% Na2SO4 + 25% NaCl)
